compacted_candidates.title: Claude-context incremental indexing unreachable via MCP tool
compacted_candidates.body: claude-context's merkle-DAG incremental indexing (reindexByChange, FileSynchronizer, SHA256 content hashing) is fully implemented but not wired to the MCP tool surface. index_codebase always does full-reindex; incremental path only runs on internal 5-min background timer inside the MCP server process. On-demand incremental indexing is not exposed to agents calling the tool.

compacted_candidates.title: SynthBrain v2 removed GitNexus symbol-extraction dependency
compacted_candidates.body: PREVIOUS: SynthBrain hard-depends on GitNexus for symbol extraction. CORRECTED TO: SynthBrain v2 uses tree-sitter directly for symbol extraction; GitNexus removed as a hard dependency. GitNexus remains optional at runtime for call-graph queries only, not for core L2/L4 generation. This makes the integration swappable (e.g., CodeGraph callers/callees as drop-in replacement).

compacted_candidates.title: Deep source audit uncovers features README-only reads miss
compacted_candidates.body: Graphify's SHA256 hash-cache incremental rebuild was not visible in README but documented in knowledge-vault atoms. README-level retrieval of cloned repos misses implementation details; verify critical claims against actual source code (config, test, implementation files) not just documentation.

compacted_candidates.title: Retrieval: inventing plausible cover stories breaks trust
compacted_candidates.body: During research synthesis, an inconsistency (`.gitnexus/kuzu/` vs. `.gitnexus/`) was "fixed" by inventing a plausible-sounding rename story ("formerly KuzuDB, now LadybugDB") without checking sources. The path never appears in the actual README. Fabrication trades off convenience for credibility; always verify uncertain claims directly against primary sources before wrapping them in explanations.

compacted_candidates.title: Nexus vs uber-db knowledge boundary (classify, never auto-write)
compacted_candidates.body: Nexus SessionEnd extraction classifies memories into promotion_target (adr/ddr/best_practice/recipe/note/none) but never auto-writes typed artifacts. Candidates surface for human review; promotion happens via existing per-file skills, which write .md files that uber-db watcher indexes automatically. Memories remain provisional/experiential knowledge only. → ADR-060.
